evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 形義通解
evidence.text: The database says the oracle, bronze, and seal forms share a construction, but the original meaning is unknown. It reports that Xu Shen interpreted the graph as heaven and earth with yin and yang crossing between them, an account followed by Zhu Fangpu; it says the graph was later commonly borrowed for the numeral. This presents the Shuowen explanation as a historical interpretation, not a confirmed account of graphic origin.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解 / competing graphic-origin proposals
evidence.text: The entry records several proposals for the graph's original motivation: Yu Shengwu treated it as a tally mark; Ding Shan identified it as an early form of 互, a cord-collecting device; Zhang Bingquan proposed an outstretched hand with visible palm lines; and Ji Xusheng took a five-horizontal-stroke form to be four plus a decorative stroke. The database questions the last proposal, citing Ji Xusheng's view that the five-stroke graph is not 五. These are attributed scholarly analyses, not a settled consensus. The database does not establish the name or pronunciation of a depicted object behind the cord-device proposal.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry cites oracle-bone inscription 合集 14316, where 五 counts dogs and sheep in a sacrificial offering, and 合集 6 for 五月. These attest numeral and ordinal uses in the oracle-bone corpus; they show use by the time of those inscriptions, not when the graph or numeral first originated.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry cites bronze-inscription uses of 五 as a numeral, including 尹姞鬲「易玉五品」, as an ordinal in 五年師…𣪕, and the phrase 五日 in another inscription. It also gives Warring States bamboo-slip uses as a numeral and place name. These examples establish later uses, but do not by themselves establish a semantic path from an earlier non-numeral meaning.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃 (Chinese Text Project), Shuowen Jiezi
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry reads: 五，五行也。从二，陰陽在天地閒交午也。凡五之屬皆从五。 This is Xu Shen's Han-era explanation connecting the graph with the Five Phases and crossing yin and yang between heaven and earth; it is evidence for his interpretation, not independent confirmation of the graph's original formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷十五 : 五部

evidence.text: Unihan gives 五 the current Mandarin reading wǔ. This is modern reading metadata and does not establish an ancient phonetic or graphic role.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E94

evidence.text: Unihan lists 五 as “five; surname,” assigns primary numeric value 5, and gives modern reading fields including kMandarin wǔ, Cantonese ng5, Japanese on GO and kun ITSUTSU, Korean O, and Vietnamese ngũ. These are lexical and reading metadata, not dated evidence for semantic chronology.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E94

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, supplementary materials
evidence.text: The authors' version 1.1 table gives 五 wǔ, Middle Chinese nguX, Old Chinese *C.ŋˤaʔ, gloss ‘five’, GSR 0058a. The supplied local row in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv agrees exactly. MC and OC are distinct columns and should not be conflated. This is a reconstruction of the numeral word's pronunciation, not evidence for an ancient object name or graphic origin.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Repository local structured reading data, checked against Unicode Consortium Unihan record
evidence.text: The supplied local row for 五 is kMandarin wǔ, matching the inspected official Unihan record for U+4E94. Local Baxter–Sagart row for 五 is py wǔ, MC nguX, OC *C.ŋˤaʔ, gloss five; it matches the authors' published table. These records concern 五 alone; this research identified no sound component in the graph requiring a component-versus-host reading comparison.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E94

gaps: The local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were checked as supplied; the corresponding upstream official pages were cited for click-through. The accessible Unihan record confirms kMandarin wǔ and the supplementary table search result confirms the Baxter–Sagart row. The directly opened Baxter–Sagart pinyin-sorted PDF returned 502, so its searchable GSR-sorted companion was used.

No inspected primary paleographic plate or original inscription image was used here. The CUHK database provides form descriptions and cited inscription identifiers; dating the cited oracle-bone examples to a specific reign or calendar year was not established from the inspected character entry.

The graph's pre-numeral meaning and the precise motivation of its original shape remain unresolved among competing proposals. Shuowen's yin-yang/heaven-earth analysis is a historical Han explanation, not demonstrated chronology.

Although some sources claim 五 was borrowed for the numeral, the inspected evidence already shows numeral use in oracle-bone inscriptions and does not establish an earlier non-numeral use. No separately earlier source word or depicted-object name was established for the proposed cord-device explanation.

The database reports expanded or borrowed readings of 五 in later texts, including as 伍, 吾, and 語 in specified manuscript contexts, but this research did not trace their earliest examples or establish a complete semantic chronology. No semantic bridge from any proposed original pictorial referent to the numeral is demonstrated.

No component-based phonetic analysis applies to 五 as researched here; the graph is treated as an independent character, so component-reading arrays and component-origin classifications are not applicable.

The Academia Sinica article PDF search result surfaced a scholarly discussion of competing constructions and cautioned against equating graph shape, original graph meaning, and word meaning, but its page could not be opened due to a fetch timeout; claims from that inaccessible full text were not relied upon.
